I found one real bug in the uncommitted changes, all in `mock/mock.go`. I only read the diff and grepped for `mutex` uses. I didn't build the code or run any tests.

**🔴 Blocking: `mock/mock.go:522`, `AssertExpectationsForObjects` panics for `Mock` values.**
- The branch changed from `obj.(Mock)` to `obj.(*Mock)`. The old branch existed to handle the deprecated form, `AssertExpectationsForObjects(t, myMock.Mock)`, where a `Mock` is passed by value.
- A `Mock` value no longer matches the new check. It falls through to `m := obj.(assertExpectationser)` at line 525, which is an unchecked assertion. `AssertExpectations` has a pointer receiver, so a `Mock` value doesn't implement the interface and the call panics.
- The new check also changes behavior for pointers. A `*Mock` is now caught by the branch and gets the "Deprecated" log message, even though passing a pointer is the supported form.
- The change was probably made because `mutex` is now a value, so `obj.(Mock)` followed by `&m` would copy a lock. The fix has to keep handling the `Mock` value case without that copy. For example, keep `obj.(Mock)` for backward compatibility and accept the `go vet` copylocks warning, or drop the case deliberately and document it as a breaking change. Changing the assertion to `*Mock` is not a safe fix.

**🟡 Important: `mock/mock.go:258`, `Mock` now holds a `sync.Mutex` by value.**
- Any code that copies a `Mock` now copies the lock, and `go vet` (copylocks) will flag it. This is an API-visible change for users who embed or copy `Mock`.
- The removed lazy initialization and the mutex reset in `On()` are otherwise safe, because a zero-value `sync.Mutex` works. The reset was itself a bug: it replaced the mutex while other goroutines might hold it.
